title: SilkyStrings — estimated opening excerpt
method: Source-only analysis: mono 22050 Hz decoding of the original Roland MP3, 8192-sample Hann STFT at 256-sample hops, nonnegative least-squares decomposition against detune-broadened harmonic templates over MIDI 36–88, and inspection of local FFT peaks and amplitude transitions. Candidate notes were screened for upper-harmonic and subharmonic errors. The opening has independent low families near 87/131 Hz (F2/C3), then 98/147/220/330 Hz (G2/D3/A3/E4), followed by 110/165/247/262 Hz (A2/E3/B3/C4). These sustained chord families are retained; the strong 785 Hz peak in the first chord is consistent with a sixth partial of C3, so it is not automatically added as another played key. Soft transitions near 2.2 and 4.3 seconds define the chord changes.
uncertainties: Original performance MIDI is unavailable. Every event here is estimated from the MP3, not an exact original MIDI event.
Velocity 100 is an explicit placeholder. Original velocities, sustain pedal, pitch bend, modulation and other controller events are unavailable and are not recovered.

Sounding pitch families do not uniquely determine played keys when oscillator octave offsets or layered tones are unknown. This transcription uses sounding fundamentals with a newly designed patch at zero overall transpose.
MP3 encoding, detuned oscillators, effects and envelope release obscure key-down and key-up times. The MIDI contains practical gates, not measured hardware key releases.
The patch is newly authored in Septum from spectral and temporal cues. It is an approximation of the named factory sound, not Roland factory SysEx or a recovered hardware preset.
The first dyad may omit real octave-doubled keys that are inseparable from oscillator harmonics. The second and third chord voicings are provisional, including the B3/C4 cluster.
Slow attack and release make onset/off estimates uncertain by roughly 100–250 ms. The excerpt ends before the next chord.

patch_design.name: APX Strings
rationale: Broad, gently beating harmonic families suggest detuned saw-like sources; one moderately spread Super Saw and one close saw supply a restrained string ensemble.
The source rises gradually and sustains through chord changes, motivating a soft amplitude attack, long release and gently opening low-pass envelope.
A quiet modulated short delay and reverb approximate the observed stereo tail.
A first Septum render rose appreciably earlier than the source in each chord; amplitude attack was lengthened from 85 to 98 to follow the slower observed swell.
uncertainties: No authenticated factory PRESET dump is available; every changed control value is an authored approximation.
The recording does not uniquely reveal oscillator topology, layer routing, filter slope, modulation or effect settings.
Modulation delay and reverb are plausible voicing choices, not identified effect settings.
A first software render informed these control adjustments. This is a conditional audio match using estimated notes, not recovered factory settings or a hardware-calibrated DSP claim.
